nodes.text: 1. Form 3 of Foreign Assets of Small Taxpayers-Disclosure scheme will be enabled shortly

2. Due dates for filing of Income Tax Returns and Audit Reports for AY 2026-27 are extended in the cases of persons mentioned at Sl.No.2 in the Table below Explanation2 to Sub-section (1) of Section 139 of Income Tax Act 1961 vide Circular No.07/2026 dated 28th September,2026.
3. Form 1 under the “Foreign Assets of Small Taxpayers Disclosure Scheme” is now available for filing.
4. ITR-1, ITR-2, ITR-3, ITR-4, ITR-5, ITR-6 and ITR-7 for AY 2026-27 are available for filing through both online and offline utilities.
5. Filing of TDS/TCS Correction Statements pertaining to Tax Year 2026-27 has been enabled.

6. Demand Management Facilitation Centre (DFC), has been set up to guide Taxpayers on issues/grievances regarding their outstanding demands. DFC may be contacted through the e-mail id: taxdemand@cpc.incometax.gov.in or on the toll-free number - 1800 309 0131 or chargeable no. 0821-6671200.
7. Excel utilities for filing Updated return for ITR-1 to 7 for AY 2022-23 as per Finance Act, 2026 are available for filing !

Patent protection can help inventors and businesses prevent unauthorized commercial use and create opportunities for licensing, assignment, and commercialization.
Protect inventions from unauthorized commercial exploitation.

Enhance the commercial value and credibility of an innovation.
Support business growth and attract potential investors.
The patent holder can prevent others from making, using, selling, offering for sale, or importing the patented invention in India, subject to applicable law.
Provides legal remedies against unauthorized use of the patented invention.
Patents can be licensed, assigned, or commercially exploited.
Patented technology can strengthen a company's intellectual property portfolio.
Patent protection can support commercialization of innovative products and processes.
For an invention to be patentable, it generally must satisfy the following requirements:
The invention must be new and not already publicly disclosed.
It must involve a technical advance or economic significance and not be obvious to a person skilled in the art.
It must be capable of being made or used in industry.
The invention must not fall within the exclusions under the Patents Act, 1970.
A patent granted in India generally remains in force for , subject to payment of the prescribed renewal fees and other applicable requirements.
20 years from the date of filing the patent application
After the patent term expires, the invention enters the public domain and the patent rights cease.
A prior-art search is conducted to assess the novelty and patentability of the invention and identify potential conflicts.
A patent specification is prepared with the required description, claims, abstract, and drawings, where applicable. Depending on the stage of development, a  may be filed.

Patent applications are ordinarily published after , subject to applicable provisions and requests for early publication.
18 months from the filing or priority date
The applicant must request examination within the prescribed period. The Patent Office examines the application and may issue objections requiring a response or amendments.
If the application satisfies the applicable legal requirements and examination objections are resolved, the patent is granted and the grant is published by the Patent Office.
